name: Pakora
description: Crispy Pakistani vegetable pakoras made with a seasoned gram-flour batter, ideal for rainy evenings and Ramadan iftar.
ingredients: ¾ tsp red chili powder, optional
method: Mix gram flour, cumin, ajwain, red chili and salt. Add water gradually, whisking to make a thick batter that coats the vegetables rather than running off them.
Add the potato, onion, green chilies and coriander and mix until evenly coated. Rest for 5–10 minutes while the oil heats.
Heat frying oil over medium heat. Test with a small drop of batter; it should rise steadily without darkening immediately.
Drop small portions of the mixture into the oil without crowding the pan. Fry over medium heat, turning as needed, until deeply golden and crisp and the potato slices inside are tender.
Drain well on a rack or kitchen paper and serve immediately with chutney.
tips: Slice potatoes thinly so they cook through before the batter becomes too dark.
If the batter becomes watery after the onions release moisture, mix in a little more gram flour.
Avoid excessively hot oil, which can brown the outside while leaving the centre undercooked.
storage: Pakoras are best fresh. Refrigerate leftovers promptly for up to 2 days and reheat in an oven or air fryer until piping hot and crisp.
